brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

finish.summary: I built a closed, portable organizer from three bases joined together: two full bases and one half base. The two full bases hold removable divided bins, and each has a top cover so parts stay in place when you carry it. The half base holds a drawer. A carry handle sits on the cover over the centre base (0,0,0). I closed every open face with an end cap and bolted the joints together (36 parts in all). For staging, I put screws, nuts and standoffs in four bin compartments and tweezers in the drawer. The bin props sit under the covers, so you can't see them in the outside view. One compartment of the two-section bin is empty because no prop would fit there. The configurator check found no rule errors and no collisions between parts. It only checks fit, not strength, so it can't tell whether the handle and joints are strong enough to carry the organizer when it's full.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
